description: Biohacking Village explores cybersecurity in healthcare, medical device security, cyberbiosecurity, FHIR APIs, open-source medicine, patient privacy, and biological citizen science.

talks.title: The Little Things
talks.teaser: Four Thieves Vinegar Collective founder Mixæl Laufer shares open-source medicine projects, decentralized hardware, and grassroots biohacking initiatives.
talks.summary:
Decentralizing Medicine and Public Health Infrastructure

The Four Thieves Vinegar Collective develops open-source, decentralized hardware and chemical synthesis pathways to liberate life-saving medications from proprietary corporate monopolies.

Grassroots Solutions to Broken Healthcare Supply Chains

Mixæl Laufer shares updates on distributed medical projects engineered to provide communities with autonomous access to emergency pharmaceuticals and harm reduction tools.

Empowering Autonomous Health Sovereignty

By releasing open-source hardware designs for chemical reactors and automated medicine dispensers, the collective empowers individuals to manufacture essential therapies locally.

The Hacker Ethic in Medical Autonomy

Laufer inspires the hacker community to apply engineering and open-source principles to solve critical healthcare and survival challenges.

talks.title: The Economics of Cybersecurity in Biomanufacturing
talks.teaser: Matt McMahon and Shannon Lantzy model economic cyber risks in biomanufacturing, demonstrating how targeted attacks threaten global vaccine production.
talks.summary:
The Strategic Importance of Biomanufacturing

The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted biomanufacturing facilities as critical national security infrastructure responsible for rapid vaccine synthesis and pharmaceutical distribution.

Modeling Cyber Threats to Biological Production Lines

Matt McMahon and Shannon Lantzy present a realistic biomanufacturing attack scenario, analyzing vulnerabilities in bioreactor telemetry, digital sequence data, and cold-chain monitoring.

The Economics of Biosecurity Disruptions

The authors evaluate the financial and public health fallout of intellectual property theft, batch contamination, and ransomware-induced production shutdowns.

Building Resilient Cyber-Biosecurity Defenses

The presentation provides biomanufacturing leaders with risk quantification models and actionable security controls to safeguard pharmaceutical pipelines.

talks.title: The Digital Physiome: Wearables and Continuous Biometrics
talks.teaser: Digital medicine researchers explore continuous biometric monitoring via consumer wearables, examining edge data processing and privacy risks.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of Continuous Biometric Monitoring

Scalable wearable sensors and edge computing now enable continuous physiological monitoring, providing unprecedented clinical insights into acute and chronic medical conditions.

Constructing the Digital Physiome

Jennifer Goldsack and Jessilyn Dunn explain how multi-sensor data streams (heart rate variability, skin temperature, pulse oximetry) are aggregated to detect early infection signatures.

Data Integrity, Security, and Patient Privacy Risks

Streaming sensitive biometric data to commercial cloud platforms creates severe privacy risks, data ownership questions, and vulnerability to adversarial telemetry manipulation.

Establishing Standards for Digital Health Technologies

The authors advocate for open verification standards and secure edge-processing frameworks to validate clinical wearable data securely.

talks.title: Securing the Internet of Biological Things
talks.teaser: Thom Dixon explores the emerging Internet of Biological Things (IoBT), examining security models for interfacing optoelectronic computers with biological substrates.
talks.summary:
The Convergence of Computing and Biological Substrates

The Internet of Biological Things (IoBT) represents the merging of digital computing with living biological systems through optogenetic circuits, bioelectrochemical interfaces, and nanosensors.

Challenging Classical Information Security Assumptions

Thom Dixon analyzes how interfacing digital microcontrollers with biological cells disrupts foundational infosec paradigms like confidentiality, integrity, and non-repudiation.

Threat Modeling Biological Communication Channels

The author explores potential attack vectors—including DNA data injection, cellular pathway jamming, and biosensor telemetry spoofing.

A Cyberbiosecurity Governance Framework

Dixon proposes an interdisciplinary governance roadmap for biologists and cybersecurity researchers to establish fail-safe architectures for bio-digital systems.

talks.title: Red vs. Blue vs. Green: Aligning Healthcare Stakeholders
talks.teaser: Vee Schmitt and Ken Kato deconstruct conflicting perspectives between medical device manufacturers (Green), attackers (Red), and hospital defenders (Blue).
talks.summary:
The Fragmented Perspectives in Medical Device Security

Securing healthcare environments involves distinct stakeholder groups—medical device manufacturers, offensive researchers, and hospital clinical engineers—who often operate with conflicting priorities.

Deconstructing Stakeholder Worldviews

Vee Schmitt and Ken Kato explore the operational constraints of each group: regulatory compliance for manufacturers, proof-of-concept impact for researchers, and patient uptime for clinicians.

Bridging the Communication and Cultural Divide

The authors analyze why traditional vulnerability disclosures frequently trigger defensive vendor friction and regulatory paralysis rather than rapid patching.

Collaborative Frameworks for Healthcare Resilience

The presentation provides actionable blueprints for establishing coordinated vulnerability disclosure channels and cross-functional medical security working groups.

talks.title: Playing with FHIR: Hacking Healthcare APIs
talks.teaser: Alissa Knight and IU Health CISO Mitch Parker demonstrate exploiting FHIR and mobile health APIs, detailing offensive kill chains and defensive remediation.
talks.summary:
The Rapid Adoption of FHIR and Mobile Health APIs

Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) APIs power modern patient portals, mobile health apps, and electronic health record (EHR) data exchanges.

Deconstructing the Healthcare API Kill Chain

Alissa Knight demonstrates systemic vulnerabilities across leading mHealth apps—including Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA), hardcoded developer keys, and unauthenticated endpoints.

Exfiltrating Protected Health Information (PHI) at Scale

Exploiting flawed API endpoints allows attackers to dump millions of patient records and medical histories without triggering perimeter WAF alarms.

Defensive Architecture and API Governance

Mitch Parker presents strategic and tactical defense maneuvers for healthcare CISOs to enforce token validation, continuous API discovery, and data integrity monitoring.

talks.title: OWASP & CSA IoT: Impacting Medical Security
talks.teaser: Aaron Guzman details how OWASP and Cloud Security Alliance IoT security guidance directly apply to securing embedded medical devices and connected healthcare.
talks.summary:
Applying Open-Source IoT Standards to Healthcare

Connected clinical equipment—from patient monitors to infusion pumps—shares foundational hardware and cloud architecture with general enterprise IoT devices.

Overview of the OWASP and CSA IoT Projects

Aaron Guzman reviews top vulnerability categories defined by the OWASP IoT Project and Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) IoT Working Group.

Remediating Common Embedded Vulnerabilities in Medical Hardware

Guzman provides practical guidance for eliminating insecure firmware update mechanisms, unencrypted communications, weak default credentials, and insecure web interfaces.

A Comprehensive Checklist for Healthcare Engineers

The presentation provides medical device developers and hospital procurement teams with an actionable security assessment checklist.

talks.title: Open Source Vaccine Developer Kits (VDKs)
talks.teaser: Alex Hoekstra introduces Open Source Vaccine Developer Kits (VDKs) to democratize infectious disease research, reduce costs, and accelerate pandemic response.
talks.summary:
The Monopolistic Cost of Proprietary Vaccine Development

Traditional vaccine development is an expensive, proprietary endeavor concentrated within a few multinational pharmaceutical corporations, limiting global equity.

Introducing Open Source Vaccine Developer Kits

Alex Hoekstra presents the concept of Vaccine Developer Kits (VDKs), modular open-source biological tools designed to streamline antigen design, expression, and testing.

Accelerating Rapid Prototyping and Biosecurity Innovation

By lowering the cost barrier and providing standardized testing protocols, VDKs empower researchers worldwide to collaborate on emerging infectious disease countermeasures.

Balancing Open-Science Innovation and Dual-Use Biosecurity

Hoekstra discusses governance models and biosecurity guardrails to ensure distributed vaccine research remains safe, equitable, and transparent.

talks.title: No Aggregation Without Representation
talks.teaser: Light Collective founder Andrea Downing explores patient data rights, corporate health data aggregation, and the urgent need for patient-led cybersecurity advocacy.
talks.summary:
Patients as the Center of Healthcare Cybersecurity

In the wake of hospital ransomware disruptions and mass health data broker aggregation, patient communities face severe privacy and clinical safety risks without a seat at the policy table.

The Exploitation of Unregulated Health Data

Andrea Downing investigates how commercial health apps, online patient support groups, and marketing trackers harvest sensitive clinical data outside HIPAA protections.

Demanding Patient Representation in Cybersecurity Governance

Downing argues for 'No Aggregation Without Representation', urging policymakers and researchers to treat patients as vital stakeholders in digital health security design.

Building Grassroots Patient Cyber Collectives

The presentation showcases the Light Collective's initiatives to train patient advocates in digital rights, vulnerability reporting, and algorithmic accountability.

talks.title: The Future State of Healthcare Cybersecurity
talks.teaser: Physician-hackers Christian Dameff and Jeff Tully synthesize lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic to outline an improved state of resilience for clinical healthcare.
talks.summary:
Lessons from Healthcare Under Pandemic Strain

The global pandemic laid bare systemic vulnerabilities across clinical health systems, where cyber disruptions directly exacerbated emergency room crowding and patient care delays.

Synthesizing Clinical Experience and Security Research

Dr. Christian Dameff and Dr. Jeff Tully examine how cybersecurity incidents impact patient morbidity, ICU workflows, and emergency transport routing.

A Roadmap for Future Healthcare Resiliency

The authors outline essential structural reforms, including establishing regional clinical cyber mutual-aid networks, subsidizing hospital security tooling, and training medical staff in cyber triage.

A Call for Continuous Researcher Engagement

The speakers urge the security community to partner with healthcare providers to build resilient, patient-centered digital health infrastructure.

talks.title: Why You Should Join the Biohacking Village
talks.teaser: BD CISO Rob Suarez highlights the mission of the Biohacking Village, inviting security researchers and clinicians to collaborate in defending healthcare.
talks.summary:
In this address at the DEF CON 29 Biohacking Village, Rob Suarez, Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) at global medical technology manufacturer Becton Dickinson (BD), makes a compelling case for collaboration between medical device makers and the hacker community. He opens at 02:00 by underscoring the profound stakes of healthcare cybersecurity, explaining that securing connected clinical devices is directly tied to preserving patient safety and human life.

Rob details three core advantages of manufacturer engagement with the Biohacking Village at 04:00: crowdsourcing specialized vulnerability research, fostering direct technical dialogue between product designers and security practitioners, and establishing transparent vulnerability disclosure frameworks. He addresses the escalating surge of ransomware and cyber threats targeting clinical environments at 06:00, emphasizing that no device manufacturer can achieve absolute security in isolation.

At 10:00, Rob outlines BD's proactive coordinated disclosure model, showing how the company routinely publishes product security bulletins, common vulnerability enumerations (CVEs), and remediation patches. He describes the collaborative Device Lab environment at 12:00, where internal engineering teams work alongside independent hackers to evaluate physical medical hardware. He finishes at 14:00 by reiterating that transparent vulnerability reporting empowers healthcare providers to protect patient care. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Internet of Ingestible Things: Security by Design
talks.teaser: Mariam Elgabry presents outcomes from the first Internet-of-Ingestible-Things workshop, establishing Security-by-Design principles for smart pills and micro-sensors.
talks.summary:
The Rise of Ingestible Smart Sensors and Drug Delivery

Ingestible medical micro-devices—such as smart pills with internal transmitters and diagnostic sensors—are entering clinical trials for targeted drug delivery and gastrointestinal imaging.

Cyber-Biosecurity Risks in Gastrointestinal Electronics

Mariam Elgabry examines the unique attack surfaces of ingestible devices, including wireless RF command injection, biosensing tampering, and unauthorized data extraction.

Collaborative Regulatory and Technical Principles

Elgabry shares consensus outcomes from an international workshop bringing together cybersecurity researchers, biomedical engineers, and medical device regulators.

Embedding Security-by-Design in Next-Gen Micro-Devices

The author outlines fundamental Security-by-Design principles, emphasizing lightweight cryptographic authentication and hardware tamper-resistance for smart pills.

talks.title: Reflections on Race, Health, and Equity
talks.teaser: Bioethics researcher Nia Johnson reflects on the systemic intersection of racial equity, public health disparities, and healthcare technology design.
talks.summary:
A Year of Reckoning in Public Health

The events of 2020 exposed deep systemic inequities in healthcare access, algorithmic bias in medical diagnostic tools, and disproportionate pandemic impacts on marginalized communities.

Analyzing Algorithmic Bias in Clinical Software

Nia Johnson examines how historical biases embedded in clinical datasets lead diagnostic algorithms and resource allocation tools to systematically disadvantage minority patients.

The Role of Technologists in Healthcare Equity

Johnson discusses how biohackers, software engineers, and healthcare leaders must critically evaluate demographic assumptions when designing medical technologies.

A Framework for Equitable Digital Health

The presentation calls for inclusive testing pipelines, diverse data representation, and ethical oversight in health technology innovation.

talks.title: Healthcare Innovation with People of All Abilities
talks.teaser: Accessibility experts Pia Zaragoza and Joel Isaac present universal design frameworks to ensure medical devices and healthcare apps are secure and accessible to all.
talks.summary:
Disability Inclusion in Digital Health

With over one billion people worldwide experiencing some form of disability, healthcare technology must be engineered to accommodate diverse physical, sensory, and cognitive abilities.

Universal Design and Digital Accessibility Principles

Pia Zaragoza and Joel Isaac walk through foundational universal design standards, evaluating how medical software interfaces often fail basic accessibility requirements.

Balancing Security Controls with Usability

The authors analyze how overly complex authentication mechanisms (such as visual CAPTCHAs or biometrics) can lock disabled patients out of life-saving medical devices.

A Practical Guide for Inclusive Healthcare Engineering

The presentation provides development teams with actionable design patterns to build accessible, secure, and intuitive digital health solutions.

talks.title: Fishing or Hunting: The CTI League
talks.teaser: CTI League founder Ohad Zaidenberg shares how a global volunteer coalition of threat intelligence analysts neutralizes cyber attacks against hospitals and medical centers.
talks.summary:
The Formation of the CTI League

In response to surging ransomware attacks on healthcare facilities during the COVID-19 pandemic, cybersecurity volunteers worldwide established the Cyber Threat Intelligence League (CTI League).

Proactive Threat Hunting for Medical Facilities

Ohad Zaidenberg details the league's operational methodology, hunting for exposed medical systems, stolen clinician credentials, and active threat actor infrastructure.

Rapid Triage and Takedown Operations

By collaborating with law enforcement and national CERTs, the CTI League neutralized hundreds of malicious domains and provided early warnings to targeted hospitals.

A Model for Global Humanitarian Cyber Defense

Zaidenberg reflects on lessons learned from coordinating over 1,500 volunteer analysts across 80 countries to defend life-saving organizations.

talks.title: Applying the Cyber Defense Matrix in Healthcare
talks.teaser: Cyber Defense Matrix creator Sounil Yu applies his logical framework to healthcare environments, categorizing clinical assets and identifying defensive gaps.
talks.summary:
Making Sense of the Complex Security Vendor Landscape

Healthcare CISOs are inundated with vendor products and regulatory requirements, making it difficult to objectively evaluate defensive coverage across clinical networks.

Understanding the Cyber Defense Matrix (CDM)

Sounil Yu explains the structure of the Cyber Defense Matrix, mapping the five NIST CSF functions (Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover) across five asset classes (Devices, Apps, Networks, Data, Users).

Mapping Healthcare Assets and Medical IoT

Yu demonstrates how hospitals can use the CDM to map specialized clinical assets—such as bedside infusion pumps, PACS imaging servers, and EHR databases.

Identifying Defensive Gaps and Optimizing Spend

The presentation illustrates how healthcare security teams can use the matrix to pinpoint architectural blind spots and rationalize security tooling investments.

talks.title: Cloud Security for Healthcare and Life Sciences
talks.teaser: Life sciences and cloud security leaders examine securing multi-tenant genomic data lakes and precision medicine platforms in public cloud environments.
talks.summary:
The Transition of Life Sciences and Genomics to the Cloud

Large-scale precision medicine initiatives (such as NIH's All of Us Research Program and AnVIL) process massive genomic sequencing datasets in public cloud platforms.

Architectural Security Controls for Genomic Data Lakes

Panelists review multi-tenant access control models, role-based identity federation, and cryptographic envelope encryption used to secure terabytes of DNA sequencing data.

Balancing Open Scientific Research with HIPAA and Patient Privacy

The discussion explores technical mechanisms for enabling authorized medical researchers to run distributed analytics while strictly preventing patient re-identification.

Best Practices for Healthcare Cloud Deployments

The panel provides cloud architects with compliance frameworks and automated governance policies for deploying secure healthcare environments.

talks.title: Chinese Military Bioweapons and Intimidation Operations
talks.teaser: RedDragon analyzes Chinese military doctrine regarding biological agents, Program 863, and supply chain dependencies in international biosecurity.
talks.summary:
Unrestricted Warfare and Biological Capabilities

Analyzing strategic doctrine from the People's Liberation Army (PLA) reveals how biological research, biotechnology supply chains, and cyber operations intersect in unrestricted warfare.

Deconstructing Program 863 and State Biotechnology Initiatives

RedDragon traces China's state-sponsored biological initiatives, examining government investments in synthetic biology, genetic data collection, and dual-use biotechnology.

Supply Chain Dependencies and Global Intimidation Strategies

The presentation examines global pharmaceutical raw material dependencies and analyzes information warfare operations surrounding public health narratives.

Strategic Countermeasures for International Biosecurity

The author discusses defensive monitoring and international treaty compliance verification to safeguard global biotechnology supply chains.

talks.title: A Talk with @BadHIPPA: Demystifying Health Privacy Law
talks.teaser: Healthcare privacy attorney Lucia Savage and the creator of @BadHIPPA debunk pervasive legal myths, clarifying what HIPAA actually regulates.
talks.summary:
The Pervasive Misunderstanding of HIPAA

During the pandemic and political debates, the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) became widely misunderstood and misquoted across social media and news broadcasts.

The Origins of the @BadHIPPA Viral Account

Lucia Savage and the creator of the popular Twitter account @BadHIPPA review some of the most absurd, hilarious, and legally inaccurate public claims about HIPAA.

What HIPAA Actually Regulates

Savage clearly explains the statutory boundaries of HIPAA, defining 'Covered Entities' (hospitals, insurers) versus commercial entities and private citizens.

Modern Health Data Privacy Gaps Beyond HIPAA

The speakers discuss critical regulatory gaps in protecting consumer health data collected by mobile wellness apps, fitness trackers, and search engines.

talks.title: A Cohort of Pirate Ships: Ethics in Biomedical Citizen Science
talks.teaser: Bioethics researcher Alex Pearlman presents empirical research on ethical attitudes, peer review preferences, and self-governance in community biohacklabs.
talks.summary:
The Rise of Biomedical Citizen Science and Biohacklabs

Community biohacking laboratories, DIY biology collectives, and citizen scientists are independently conducting genetic engineering, diagnostics development, and open-source therapeutics.

Empirical Research on Biohacker Ethical Attitudes

Alex Pearlman presents newly published research surveying citizen scientists and biohackers on ethical oversight, risk assessment, and peer review preferences.

Overcoming the 'Pirate Ship' Stereotype

While critics often stereotype community labs as unregulated pirate ships, survey data reveals robust grassroots ethical deliberation and informal peer review mechanisms.

Policy Roadmaps for Inclusive Bioethics Oversight

Pearlman proposes cooperative governance models bridging academic Institutional Review Boards (IRBs) and decentralized community biohacking groups.
